newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Adequacy ratio for Kuwaiti banks reaches 27.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Adequacy ratio for Kuwaiti banks reaches 27.4 pct.

text.p: Kuwait's Central Bank governor said in remarks published on Tuesday that local banks achieved a capital adequacy ratio of 27.4 percent at the end of June 1996, far exceeding the minimum of eight percent.
"It is difficult to say that at the time being there are weak banks in Kuwait," Governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al-Sabah told al-Rai al-Aam newspaper.
Kuwait has six commercial banks, two specialised banks, an Islamic finance institution and a branch of a Bahrain-based bank.
Sheikh Salem said combined profits of Kuwaiti banks in 1993, 1994 and 1995 were 115.9 million dinars ($388 million), 95.5 million and 129 million dinars, respectively.
He advised some banks to "seriously" consider merging to boost their competitive edge on the domestic and international markets.
Sheikh Salem said the Central Bank has started work on a new draft law to govern operations by Islamic banks in Kuwait but did not say when it would be presented to parliament.
